evidence.detail: elif name and d.get('archetype_name') and name == d.get('archetype_name', '').lower() — compares titlecased name ('White Jund') to lowercase archetype name ('white jund'); these are never equal so the skip-normalization branch never fires

When the archetype check fails, normalize_colors() runs; it finds 'White' (W) and 'Jund' (BRG) as color words, combines to WBRG, canonicalizes to 'BRGW' (no proper 4-color name), replaces 'White' with 'BRGW' and removes 'Jund' — resulting in just 'BRGW'
COLOR_COMBINATIONS has 'BRGW': ['B','R','G','W'] — confirms 4-color WBRG combination has no proper name, so name_from_colors returns 'BRGW'

triage.fix_sketch: In decksite/deck_name.py:106, change `name == d.get('archetype_name', '').lower()` to `name.lower() == d.get('archetype_name', '').lower()`. This makes the skip-normalization check case-insensitive so decks whose names exactly match their archetype (e.g. 'White Jund' with archetype 'White Jund') correctly bypass color normalization. Add a test case in deck_name_test.py.
triage.notes: The intent of the existing check is clear — skip normalization when name matches archetype — but a case mismatch makes it a no-op. The one-character fix aligns behavior with intent. Existing tests in deck_name_test.py provide coverage to guard against regressions.
